Abalone Shell-Ring Counts

Source: R/data-abalone_rings.R
abalone_rings.Rd

Counts of shell growth rings and physical measurements of 4,177 blacklip abalone (Haliotis rubra) from Tasmania, Australia, from the UCI Machine Learning Repository Abalone dataset. The number of rings is an integer count that is roughly equidispersed overall but conditionally underdispersed given the size measurements, which makes it a useful example for the dispersion-flexible count distributions in this package.

Usage

abalone_rings

Format

A data frame with 4,177 rows (one per abalone) and 9 columns:

sex

Factor with levels F (female), I (infant) and M (male). Source name Sex.

length

Longest shell measurement, in millimeters divided by 200. Source name Length.

diameter

Shell diameter perpendicular to the length, in millimeters divided by 200. Source name Diameter.

height

Height with meat in the shell, in millimeters divided by 200. Source name Height.

whole_weight

Weight of the whole abalone, in grams divided by 200. Source name Whole weight.

shucked_weight

Weight of the meat, in grams divided by 200. Source name Shucked weight.

viscera_weight

Gut weight after bleeding, in grams divided by 200. Source name Viscera weight.

shell_weight

Shell weight after drying, in grams divided by 200. Source name Shell weight.

rings

Number of shell rings (integer, 1 to 29). The count response. Source name Rings.

Source

Nash, W., Sellers, T., Talbot, S., Cawthorn, A. and Ford, W. (1994). Abalone (dataset). UCI Machine Learning Repository. doi:10.24432/C55C7W . Archive https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/1/abalone.zip (retrieved 2026-11-17).

Details

The observation unit is one abalone. In the source, examples with missing values were removed (most of them missing the ring count) and the continuous measurements were divided by 200; the stored values keep that scaling. The data were collected for a 1994 population-biology study and should not be treated as representative of current populations.

Preparation for this package (script data-raw/abalone_rings.R in the source repository, which checks the SHA-256 hashes of the publisher's archive and data file): columns renamed to lower-case snake_case, sex stored as a factor and rings as an integer. No rows were removed and no values were changed.

Data-quality notes: two abalone have height equal to 0 and one has height 1.13 (226 mm), far above all others; check these before using logarithms of the measurements. The age in years is often approximated as rings + 1.5; that derived age is not a count and should not be used as a predictor of rings. The absence of zero counts reflects the biology (every abalone has at least one ring), not a zero-truncated sampling design.

References

Nash, W. J., Sellers, T. L., Talbot, S. R., Cawthorn, A. J. and Ford, W. B. (1994). The population biology of abalone (Haliotis species) in Tasmania. I. Blacklip abalone (H. rubra) from the north coast and islands of Bass Strait. Sea Fisheries Division, Technical Report No. 48.

Examples

data("abalone_rings", package = "flexCountReg")
str(abalone_rings)
#> 'data.frame':	4177 obs. of  9 variables:
#>  $ sex           : Factor w/ 3 levels "F","I","M": 3 3 1 3 2 2 1 1 3 1 ...
#>  $ length        : num  0.455 0.35 0.53 0.44 0.33 0.425 0.53 0.545 0.475 0.55 ...
#>  $ diameter      : num  0.365 0.265 0.42 0.365 0.255 0.3 0.415 0.425 0.37 0.44 ...
#>  $ height        : num  0.095 0.09 0.135 0.125 0.08 0.095 0.15 0.125 0.125 0.15 ...
#>  $ whole_weight  : num  0.514 0.226 0.677 0.516 0.205 ...
#>  $ shucked_weight: num  0.2245 0.0995 0.2565 0.2155 0.0895 ...
#>  $ viscera_weight: num  0.101 0.0485 0.1415 0.114 0.0395 ...
#>  $ shell_weight  : num  0.15 0.07 0.21 0.155 0.055 0.12 0.33 0.26 0.165 0.32 ...
#>  $ rings         : int  15 7 9 10 7 8 20 16 9 19 ...
c(mean = mean(abalone_rings$rings), var = var(abalone_rings$rings))
#>      mean       var 
#>  9.933684 10.395266 

# \donttest{
fit <- countreg(rings ~ sex + length + diameter + shell_weight,
                data = abalone_rings, family = "POISSON", method = "BFGS")
summary(fit)
#> Call:
#> countreg(formula = rings ~ sex + length + diameter + shell_weight, 
#>     data = abalone_rings, family = "POISSON", method = "BFGS")
#> 
#> Model: countreg | family: POISSON | optimizer: BFGS
#> Iterations: 3 
#> Convergence: successful convergence 
#> 
#> Coefficients (standard errors: Hessian-based):
#>              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)    1.9801     0.0390   50.81  < 2e-16 ***
#> sexI          -0.1197     0.0151   -7.93  2.2e-15 ***
#> sexM          -0.0140     0.0114   -1.22     0.22    
#> length        -1.0483     0.2461   -4.26  2.1e-05 ***
#> diameter       1.5894     0.3100    5.13  3.0e-07 ***
#> shell_weight   1.0014     0.0755   13.26  < 2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Log-likelihood: -9751.611 | AIC: 19515.22 | BIC: 19553.25 
#> N: 4177
# Conditional dispersion: the Pearson statistic per degree of freedom is
# well below 1, i.e. the counts are underdispersed given the predictors
mu <- predict(fit, type = "response")
sum((abalone_rings$rings - mu)^2 / mu) / (nrow(abalone_rings) - 6)
#> [1] 0.6119697
# }
